docs.title: nestedscales (Python)
docs.text:
Python binding of the R package nestedscales: multi-level discrete scales for modelling. A scale records its finest units (atoms) and their membership in coarser levels (frames) -- nested, cross-cutting or partially covered -- and data is recast between levels through the atoms, with an explicit, direction-aware rule per value column.

import pyarrow as pa
import nestedscales as ns

s = ns.scale_example()
print(s)

d = pa.table({"unit": ["U1", "U2", "U3", "U4", "U5", "U6"],
              "capacity": [1.0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]})
ns.recast_scale(d, s, source="unit", target="sector", rule="sum")  # aggregate
y = pa.table({"sector": ["P", "S"], "capacity": [10.0, 20]})
ns.recast_scale(y, s, source="sector", target="class", rule="sum",
                weight="size")                                     # split by weight
ns.join_scale(d, s, attach=True)                                  # attach labels

docs.title: One API, several languages
docs.text:
Every function has the same name and argument order as in R, and is a free function (ns.scale_frames(s), not s.frames()). API.md at the repository root is the shared specification. Python-specific spellings:

  • the source/target arguments are source and target, the agreed names for every binding; R still spells them from/to until 0.2.0;
  • R's summary(x) is scale_summary(x);
  • a logical with an offenders/sizes attribute is a Verdict, which is truthy and compares equal to a bool.

Error and warning messages are the R package's, verbatim apart from the argument names. Correctness is checked against R: specs/goldens/generate.R writes several hundred cases from the R source, and the test suite replays every one.

docs.title: Data backends
docs.text:
The engine computes on pyarrow. Inputs may be a pyarrow.Table, pandas, polars or a dict of columns, and results come back in the caller's type. A pyarrow.dataset.Dataset or polars LazyFrame is lazy: only the needed columns are scanned, batch=/batch_by= push a filter into the scan, and without collect=True the result holds the observed target units only, as in R.

Dimension packages build on the public backend_* functions (backend_of, backend_scan, backend_restore, ...) to accept the same inputs and return the caller's type.

docs.title: Stores shared with R
docs.text: write_scale_dataset() / open_scale_dataset() read and write the R package's store -- hive-partitioned Arrow IPC data plus a JSON manifest and Arrow leaftables (a legacy YAML manifest is still read) -- so data and its scales move between R and Python unchanged. write_scale() / read_scale() exchange single definition files and bundles (JSON header; inline, Arrow or CSV tables), and read_scale("carriers") opens the fuel taxonomy vendored with the binding (scale_catalog() lists every registered definition). Scales written by R's timescales and geoscales are restored as Calendars and GeoScales by the Python timescales and geoscales packages (as_calendar(), as_geoscale()).

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Ported: the scale class, construction, navigation, rules, maps, the whole recast engine (recast_scale, recast_crosswalk, recast_to_atoms, recast_from_atoms), filter/prune/share/join, 1-D arrays, the dataset store, and the ScaleProduct container. R only for now: recast_product() and the other product verbs, reconcile_scale(), and clustering.

docs.title: Scales
docs.text: Build a scale and read its structure.

docs.title: scale_from_leaftable
docs.text:
scale_from_leaftable(
    leaftable: Any,
    frames: str | Sequence[str],
    key: str | None = None,
    weights: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    default_weight: str | None = None,
    members: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]] | None = None,
    name: str = "",
    desc: str = "",
    attributes: Any = None,
    aliases: Any = None,
    **meta: Any,
) -> NestedScale

Build a NestedScale from a flat table of atoms.

leaftable has one row per atom, one column per name in frames (coarsest first) and optionally numeric weight columns. Blank strings in frame columns become null: that atom has no code at that frame.

key defaults to "unit" when that column exists, else the finest frame. weights defaults to every numeric column that is neither a frame, the key, nor a reserved name. members defaults to first-appearance order. Extra keyword arguments are merged into meta (e.g. source, labels).

docs.title: scale_example
docs.text:
scale_example() -> NestedScale

A small example scale with three awkward real-world features.

  • a code ("G1") reused at two frames, so lookups must name the frame;
  • a non-nesting pair -- group "GB" draws units from two classes;
  • a unit ("OTH") with no code at any coarser frame.

docs.title: scale_class
docs.text:
NestedScale -- the dimension-agnostic core type (port of R/scale-class.R).

A NestedScale is a nested partition of a set of atoms, in any dimension:

  • leaftable -- one row per atom: a column per frame, a unique key column (named by key) and zero or more numeric weight columns
  • frames -- frame names, COARSEST first
  • members -- frame -> the ordered code vocabulary at that frame
  • key -- name of the atom key column (default "unit")
  • meta -- name, desc, weights, default_weight, residuals, labels, source, and the sample bookkeeping (coverage, parent_totals, parent_name)

Frames are partitions of the atoms, not necessarily a tree; conversion always routes through the atoms. Anything derivable is computed on demand.

Collapse to a coarser frame: frame becomes the atom layer.

docs.title: Conversion
docs.text: Recast data between resolutions, attach labels, and declare rules.

docs.title: recast_scale
docs.text:
recast_scale(
    data: Any,
    x: NestedScale,
    source: str | None = None,
    target: str | NestedScale | None = None,
    key: str | None = None,
    values: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    rule: str | Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    weight: str | Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    na_action: NaAction = "drop",
    parent: str | None = None,
    collect: bool | None = None,
    diagnostics: Diagnostics = "auto",
    missing_sources: MissingSources = "na",
    batch: int | None = None,
    batch_by: str | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> Any

Recast values from one resolution to another.

The central conversion verb. Takes a table keyed by unit code at frame source and returns one keyed at target, aggregating (fine to coarse) or disaggregating (coarse to fine) with one rule per value column. Frames that cross-cut work too: the route always goes through the atoms. A crosswalk registered with register_scale_map() short-circuits it.

Columns that are neither the key nor a value column are identifiers (a year, a technology) and are preserved as groups, so panel data recasts in one call. Columns named like the scale's frames are dropped.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data The table: pyarrow, pandas, polars, a dict of columns, or a lazy pyarrow Dataset / polars LazyFrame. Returned in the same type. x The scale the codes in data belong to. source Frame of the codes. None infers it: key when that is a frame, else the single frame name among the data's columns. target Target frame of x, or another named scale (its atom layer is the target, matched on shared atom keys). key The code column of data. Defaults to source when that column exists, else the scale's key. values Value columns. Default: every numeric column other than the key and the frame columns; numeric identifiers (year) must be excluded by naming the values. rule One of SCALE_RULES for every value column, or a dict per column. None looks each column up with get_scale_rule(); a column with no rule anywhere is an error. weight Weight column for sum splits and weighted_mean; one name or a dict per column. None uses the registered weight, else the scale's default; with no declared weights every atom weighs 1. na_action Atoms with no code at source or target: "drop" (with a warning), "error", or "keep" (an explicit null row, so totals conserve). parent Rule "share" only: the frame the shares are taken within. Default: target when it differs from source, else the frame above. collect Lazy inputs: True materialises and completes the result; otherwise only the observed target units are returned. diagnostics The checks that scan the data (unknown codes, dropped shares, missing sources): "auto" runs them on eager inputs only; "on"/"off" force. missing_sources "na": a target whose sources are only partly present is null. "ignore": aggregate whatever is there (faster, opt-in). batch, batch_by Process in chunks of at most batch values of the identifier column batch_by (default: the first identifier). Chunking by an identifier leaves the numbers unchanged. **kwargs Passed to scale_map().

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: The recast table in the input's type, columns target, identifiers, values. Rule "share" keeps the source key and returns each value as a share of its parent-group total.

docs.title: recast
docs.text:
recast_scale() -- the central conversion verb (port of R/recast.R).

Aggregation and disaggregation are one operation. Every conversion routes through the atom layer; the route is collapsed into a small crosswalk by scale_map(), so the converter is one join plus one grouped aggregation.

The split factor is fixed for every dimension:

f = w / w_from        when the crosswalk carries weights
f = n_overlap/n_from  otherwise (the equal split)

NA semantics follow R exactly: aggregates do NOT skip nulls (a null member makes its group null), and a target whose sources are only partly present in the data is null (the partial-source poisoning law).

docs.title: recast
docs.text:
recast(
    x: Any, scale: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any
) -> Any

Recast data x through scale, dispatching on the scale's class.

For a NestedScale the arguments are those of recast_scale(): target is the target frame (or scale) and source the source frame, inferred when omitted. Dimension packages register methods with recast.register(TheirClass).

docs.title: recast_crosswalk
docs.text:
recast_crosswalk(
    data: Any,
    map: Any,
    source: str,
    target: str,
    key: str | None = None,
    values: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    rule: str | Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    ids: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    by: Sequence[str] = (),
    targets: Sequence[str | None] | None = None,
    missing_sources: MissingSources = "na",
    unit: str = "unit",
    collect: bool | None = None,
) -> Any

Recast values through a given crosswalk.

map has one row per (source, target) pair: the codes in columns source and target, n_from, n_overlap, optionally w (weighted-mean weight; default n_overlap) and w_from (with both, sum splits by w / w_from; otherwise by n_overlap / n_from), and any by columns.

docs.title: recast_from_atoms
docs.text:
recast_from_atoms(
    data: Any,
    x: NestedScale,
    target: str,
    key: str | None = None,
    values: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    rule: str | Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    weight: str | None = None,
    na_rm: bool = False,
    na_action: NaAction = "drop",
    collect: bool | None = None,
) -> Any

Aggregate atom-keyed data UP into the units of frame target.

weight names a column of the data to weight by (so it may vary by identifier); None uses a weight column if present, else the scale's declared weight. With na_rm=True a null member says nothing rather than making its group null. Unlike recast_scale(), a missing atom simply does not contribute (no partial-source poisoning).

    parent: str | None = None,
    collect: bool | None = None,
    diagnostics: Diagnostics = "auto",
    missing_sources: MissingSources = "na",
    batch: int | None = None,
    batch_by: str | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> Any

Recast values from one resolution to another.

The central conversion verb. Takes a table keyed by unit code at frame source and returns one keyed at target, aggregating (fine to coarse) or disaggregating (coarse to fine) with one rule per value column. Frames that cross-cut work too: the route always goes through the atoms. A crosswalk registered with register_scale_map() short-circuits it.

Columns that are neither the key nor a value column are identifiers (a year, a technology) and are preserved as groups, so panel data recasts in one call. Columns named like the scale's frames are dropped.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data The table: pyarrow, pandas, polars, a dict of columns, or a lazy pyarrow Dataset / polars LazyFrame. Returned in the same type. x The scale the codes in data belong to. source Frame of the codes. None infers it: key when that is a frame, else the single frame name among the data's columns. target Target frame of x, or another named scale (its atom layer is the target, matched on shared atom keys). key The code column of data. Defaults to source when that column exists, else the scale's key. values Value columns. Default: every numeric column other than the key and the frame columns; numeric identifiers (year) must be excluded by naming the values. rule One of SCALE_RULES for every value column, or a dict per column. None looks each column up with get_scale_rule(); a column with no rule anywhere is an error. weight Weight column for sum splits and weighted_mean; one name or a dict per column. None uses the registered weight, else the scale's default; with no declared weights every atom weighs 1. na_action Atoms with no code at source or target: "drop" (with a warning), "error", or "keep" (an explicit null row, so totals conserve). parent Rule "share" only: the frame the shares are taken within. Default: target when it differs from source, else the frame above. collect Lazy inputs: True materialises and completes the result; otherwise only the observed target units are returned. diagnostics The checks that scan the data (unknown codes, dropped shares, missing sources): "auto" runs them on eager inputs only; "on"/"off" force. missing_sources "na": a target whose sources are only partly present is null. "ignore": aggregate whatever is there (faster, opt-in). batch, batch_by Process in chunks of at most batch values of the identifier column batch_by (default: the first identifier). Chunking by an identifier leaves the numbers unchanged. **kwargs Passed to scale_map().

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: The recast table in the input's type, columns target, identifiers, values. Rule "share" keeps the source key and returns each value as a share of its parent-group total.

Aggregate atom-keyed data UP into the units of frame target.

weight names a column of the data to weight by (so it may vary by identifier); None uses a weight column if present, else the scale's declared weight. With na_rm=True a null member says nothing rather than making its group null. Unlike recast_scale(), a missing atom simply does not contribute (no partial-source poisoning).

scale_map(
    x: NestedScale,
    source: str,
    target: str,
    weight: str | None = None,
    by: Sequence[str] = (),
    **kwargs: object,
) -> pa.Table

Crosswalk between two frames of a scale.

One row per pair of overlapping units with n_from (atoms in the source unit), n_overlap (atoms shared), w (weight of the overlap) and w_from (full weight of the source unit); w / w_from is the split share of sum disaggregation. The label columns are named by the frames; a null target marks atoms target does not cover. A registered map is returned as-is.
